target:: creature touched or all creatures within 5 ft.; see text
duration:: 1 minute/level
saving-throw:: Will negates (harmless)
spell-resistance:: yes (harmless)
Description
A shimmering mantle of light shrouds the subject, casting light like a torch. The subject of the spell gains a +1 resistance bonus on all saving throws per four caster levels (maximum +5 at 20th level). The subject can end the wrathful mantle at any time as a swift action to deal 2d8 points of force damage to all creatures within 5 feet.

Resource-Material/spells/w/wrathful-weap.title: wrathful-weapon
Resource-Material/spells/w/wrathful-weap.content:
Wrathful Weapon
source:: Advanced Class Origins pg. 31
school:: transmutation [see text]
level:: cleric 4, oracle 4, warpriest 4
Casting
casting-time:: 1 standard action
components:: V, S, DF
Effect
range:: touch
target:: melee weapon touched (see text)
duration:: 1 minute/level
saving-throw:: Will (harmless, object)
spell-resistance:: yes (object)
Description
You grant the targeted weapon one of the following weapon special abilities: anarchic, axiomatic, holy, or unholy. If anarchic, this spell has the chaos descriptor; if axiomatic, the law descriptor; if holy, the good descriptor; and if unholy, the evil descriptor. If the caster attempts to place a special ability on a weapon that already has that special ability, the spell fails.
If a warpriest casts this spell on his sacred weapon, the duration doubles. Warpriests with unarmed strike as a sacred weapon can cast this spell on their unarmed strike.

Resource-Material/spells/w/wreath-of-bla.title: wreath-of-blades
Resource-Material/spells/w/wreath-of-bla.content:
Wreath of Blades
source:: Ultimate Combat pg. 249
school:: abjuration
level:: arcanist 5, bloodrager 4, magus 4, occultist 4, psychic 5, sorcerer 5, summoner 5, summoner (unchained) 5, witch 5, wizard 5
Casting
casting-time:: 1 standard action
components:: V, S, F (four mithral daggers, each worth at least 502 gp each)
Effect
range:: personal
target:: you
area:: 5-foot-radius emanation centered on you
duration:: 1 round/level
saving-throw:: Reflex half (special, see below)
spell-resistance:: no (special, see below)
Description
The daggers serving as focus of this spell take on a deadly sharpness as they animate and spin around you, creating a 5-foot-radius emanation of spinning mithral blades that moves with you. Any creature that starts its turn within the area of the spinning blades takes 1d4 points of damage for every two caster levels (maximum 10d4 at 20th level) and the damage bypasses DR/silver.
Furthermore, the daggers ward off some attacks, in a way similar to the warding weapon spell. While subject to this spell, you do not provoke attacks of opportunity for casting spells, even from creatures with the Disruptive feat. Creatures with the Spellbreaker feat can easily bypass this defensive property, though they still take damage from the spell. Your casting (even failing to cast defensively) still provokes attacks of opportunity from creatures with that feat.
Lastly, the blades that serve as the focus for this spell can be enchanted for greater effect. When all of the blades share the same enhancement bonus and special weapon qualities, a creature that is damaged by this spell is also treated as if hit by one of these weapons. For example, if a 12th-level magus casts this spell using four +1 frost mithral daggers as focus, the damage dealt by the blades would be 6d4+1 plus 1d6 cold damage, as long as the daggers were commanded to be sheathed in ice. No matter the modifications made to the focus weapons, they must always be mithral daggers. No other type of weapons can serve as a focus for this spell.

Resource-Material/spells/y/yellow-sign.title: yellow-sign
Resource-Material/spells/y/yellow-sign.content:
Yellow Sign
source:: Pathfinder #110: The Thrushmoor Terror pg. 72
school:: enchantment (compulsion) (mind-affecting)
level:: arcanist 9, bard 6, cleric 9, oracle 9, skald 6, sorcerer 9, witch 9, wizard 9 (Hastur)
Casting
casting-time:: 10 minutes
components:: V, S, M (ochre and sulfur, plus powdered gold worth a total of 15,000 gp)
Effect
range:: 0 ft.; see text
effect:: one symbol
duration:: see text
saving-throw:: Will negates
spell-resistance:: yes
Description
This spell functions as per symbol of death, save that creatures that succumb to this spell become dominated (as per dominate monster) by Hastur. This causes such creatures to seek to aid any obvious minions or worshipers of Hastur in sight, and any true worshiper of Hastur can command the affected creatures as if that worshiper had been the one to dominate them. In the case of conflicting commands issued from different true worshipers of Hastur, the commanders must attempt opposed Charisma checks, with the winner being able to command the targets for that round. If no worshipers or agents of Hastur are in sight, an affected creature can act normally. When affected by this spell’s Yellow Sign in this way, the effects last for 1 round per level. Once triggered, the Yellow Sign remains active for 10 minutes per caster level.
There is a 1% chance when a creature fails its saving throw against this spell that Hastur takes note and, for reasons of his own, decides to control the target personally. In this case, the actions taken by the dominated creature are left to the GM to determine, but the effects of this spell’s Yellow Sign persist for 1 day per level and the commands issued cannot be countermanded by any other creature, even if they are Hastur worshipers.
Regardless of how long the effects last or whether Hastur directly controls a victim, if a creature failed to resist this spell’s effects, Hastur can target that victim for the rest of its life with his fulvous dreams ability (Pathfinder RPG Bestiary 4 140). Whether or not the Great Old One ever chooses to do so is left to the GM to determine.
Yellow Sign can be made permanent with a permanency spell by a caster of 18th level or higher for the cost of 40,000 gp.

Resource-Material/spells/y/youthful-appe.title: youthful-appearance
Resource-Material/spells/y/youthful-appe.content:
Youthful Appearance
source:: Ultimate Magic pg. 249
school:: transmutation (polymorph)
level:: alchemist 1, arcanist 1, bard 1, investigator 1, medium 1, occultist 1, psychic 1, redmantisassassin 1, skald 1, sorcerer 1, witch 1, wizard 1
Casting

components:: V, S
Effect
range:: touch
target:: creature touched
duration:: 1 hour/level

You make your target look like a younger version of itself. You select how much younger it looks (for example, “10 years” or “as a young adult”). You cannot otherwise change details of the target’s appearance other than those directly associated with aging (for example, gray hair returns to its original color). The target cannot appear so much younger that it changes size. This spell does not affect any age-based modifications to ability scores or other age-related effects.

Resource-Material/spells/z/zephyrs-fleet.title: zephyrs-fleetness

Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-foul-.title: zone-of-foul-flames
Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-foul-.content:
Zone of Foul Flames
source:: Inner Sea Magic pg. 63
school:: transmutation
level:: druid 4, hunter 4
Casting
casting-time:: 1 standard action
components:: V, S, M (a sliver of tree bark from a burnt tree from the Uskwood)
Effect
range:: close (25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels)
area:: 20-ft.-radius spread
duration:: 1 minute/level
saving-throw:: Will negates
spell-resistance:: yes
Description
The twisted druids of the Uskwood forsook fire in ages past for the glory of Zon-Kuthon. Despite this aversion, these servants of Nidal know well the sting of flame, and have learned to turn it back on those that wield it. This spell creates a zone where magical fire effects twist and lash out against those who create the effects. A zone of foul flames looks unremarkable to the casual observer, but a Perception check (DC = 20 + the caster’s level) reveals a faint rippling effect in the area, as if of heat distortions in the air.
Whenever a creature casts a spell with the fire descriptor or activates a magical fire effect (as from a magic item or a special attack) while that creature is located in a zone of foul flames, that creature takes full fire damage from the effect. If the effect allows a saving throw to reduce the damage, the victim may attempt the same saving throw to reduce the damage. All creatures in a zone of foul flames gain a +4 circumstance bonus on all saving throws against fire effects, except for those made by a creature attempting to save against fire damage from his own magic. Nonmagical fire in a zone of foul flames burns half as brightly but is otherwise not affected.

Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-silen.title: zone-of-silence
Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-silen.content:
Zone of Silence
source:: PRPG Core Rulebook pg. 371
school:: illusion (glamer)
level:: bard 4, mesmerist 4, skald 4
Casting
casting-time:: 1 round
components:: V, S
Effect
range:: personal
area:: 5-ft.-radius emanation centered on you
duration:: 1 hour/level (D)
Description
By casting zone of silence, you manipulate sound waves in your immediate vicinity so that you and those within the spell’s area can converse normally, yet no one outside can hear your voices or any other noises from within, including language-dependent or sonic spell effects. This effect is centered on you and moves with you. Anyone who enters the zone immediately becomes subject to its effects, but those who leave are no longer affected. Note, however, that a successful DC 20 Linguistics check to read lips can still reveal what’s said inside a zone of silence.

Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-truth.title: zone-of-truth
Resource-Material/spells/z/zone-of-truth.content:
Zone of Truth
source:: PRPG Core Rulebook pg. 371
school:: enchantment (compulsion) (mind-affecting)
level:: cleric 2, inquisitor 2, medium 2, oracle 2, paladin 2, psychic 2, warpriest 2, witch 2

Creatures within the emanation area (or those who enter it) can’t speak any deliberate and intentional lies. Royal-Crown-of-Eldoria.title: Royal Crown of Eldoria
Royal-Crown-of-Eldoria.content:
Faction / Ruling Authority
Overview
The Royal Crown of Eldoria is the governing power of the unified kingdom of Emberfall. Formed after the Great Dragon War, it presents itself as the guarantor of peace, stability, and survival beneath the Fool’s Curtain.
Its authority extends over all former kingdoms, including Eldoria, Atheria, and Valoria.
Structure

Monarch: King Balfour IV
Military: Royal Navy, Crown Guard, specialized arcane divisions
Clergy & Orders: Includes paladins such as Caldus
Bureaucracy: Regional governors, inspectors, and Crown caretakers bananas

Public Doctrine
The Crown teaches that:

Unity is the only defense against existential threats
Dangerous knowledge and technology must be controlled
Sacrifice is sometimes necessary for the greater good

The Crown strictly regulates arcane devices capable of affecting the Fool’s Curtain.
Known Policies

Heavy taxation to fund defense and research
Strict oversight of arcane research and inventors
Classification and seizure of dangerous artifacts
Suppression of unrest and rebellion

Military Capabilities
The Crown is known to possess:

Advanced naval warships
Arcane siege weapons

the Sunlance Crystal


Experimental devices designed to control or suppress large-scale threats

the Peace Ordinance



The full extent of its arsenal is unknown.
Relationship with the People
Public loyalty to the Crown remains strong in many regions, particularly Valoria. However:

Discontent simmers among laborers and miners
Peripheral regions report harsher enforcement
Refugees such as the Fogborn face systemic discrimination

Recent History

Crackdown on unrest following events in Razor Ridge
Increased activity in Eldorian territories
Military intervention in Lowhaven

Reputation
To supporters, the Crown is the last line between civilization and annihilation.
To critics, it is an authoritarian regime willing to enforce peace at catastrophic cost.
See Also

Sunlance Crystal
Peace Ordinance
Fool’s Curtain
The Scouring of Lowhaven

Salty-Marrow.title: Salty Marrow
Salty-Marrow.content:
Salty Marrow is a crewmate of The Silver Vulture and serves as an appointed inland guide for the Heroes following the Vulture’s Bargain at the wreckage of the Wreck Island.
He is a maritime survivor of the outer curtain routes — a man who has spent too long between salvage law, pirate accords, and the creeping ecological collapse surrounding the Fool’s Curtain.
Despite his rough trade background, he does not present as cruel or predatory. Instead, he is unsettlingly calm about systemic decay, as if it is simply weather he has learned to sail through.

Role in the Campaign

Guide from sea salvage zones into inland Spire territories
Interpret regional pirate salvage law
Provide commentary on burial barges and Curtain activity
Serve as narrative contrast between “economic pragmatism” and “cosmic horror”


Personality

Dry humor under pressure
Calm acceptance of horrific systems
Quietly observant
Avoids direct moral judgment unless pushed
Speaks as though catastrophe is routine bureaucracy

He does not deny suffering.
He simply refuses to be surprised by it.

Appearance

Weather-worn naval coat reinforced with stitched tarcloth
Salt-crusted beard and brows
One eye slightly clouded (old injury or exposure to Curtain mist)
Carries salvage tags and chain tokens for legal claims


Accent / Speech Style
Salty Marrow speaks with a light Canadian cadence, softened vowels, and understated phrasing.
He often sounds like he is:

apologizing for reality itself
mildly inconvenienced by apocalypse
trying not to be dramatic about very dramatic things


Dialogue Samples
First Meeting (The Silver Vulture Bargain)

“Right then… I’ll be honest with you folks, I’ve seen worse wrecks. Not many, mind you. But worse ones. Usually they’re still moving, which is… less pleasant.”


“Name’s Marrow. Salty Marrow. Don’t ask about the first name, it’s not important and neither is my birth certificate anymore.”


“We’re offering you a clean deal. Clean-ish. Clean enough that no one gets eaten by paperwork later, anyway.”


On the Dragon-Gold Hoard

“That gold’s… well, it’s not so much currency anymore as it is a kind of emotional hazard. Long exposure to dragon presence does that.”


“You try to sell it, and people start wanting it in ways that are… not economically healthy.”


On the Burial Barges

“They call it passage. Real gentle word for it. Passage sounds like you’re going somewhere pleasant.”


“Truth is, those barges don’t really arrive anywhere. They just… stop being a problem for whoever built the system.”


“Which I suppose is one way to define spirituality. Not my preferred one, but I’m not writing the brochures.”


On the Fool’s Curtain

“That thing out there? That’s not weather. It’s more like… accumulated decisions nobody wanted to keep track of anymore.”


“You don’t sail through it. You get filed into it.”


On the Savage Spire

“Spire folk’ll tell you it’s sacred. Everything’s sacred if you say it enough times, I find.”


“Me, I think it’s just very tall and very committed to not falling down yet.”


Secrets (DM Only)

Salty Marrow has previously guided groups that never returned from the Spire
He is aware the Curtain is structural, not merely environmental
He suspects the burial barges are part of a long-term ecological “load balancing” system
He will quietly encourage the party toward truths, but never force revelation


Hooks

May reappear later as an intermediary between inland and maritime factions
Could become morally compromised if the party pushes salvage law too far
May eventually refuse service if Malazar-related corruption intensifies again

Sanctum_Map_Engine_Guide.title: Sanctum_Map_Engine_Guide
Sanctum_Map_Engine_Guide.content:
Sunken Sanctum: Map Engine Guide
Welcome to the Sunken Sanctum Engine. This tool is designed for high-speed map creation, featuring a dynamic terrain system, custom platform pathing, and a portable export format for live tabletop sessions.
🛠️ Editor Toolbar Reference
Terrain Painting

Color Palette (Wall, Floor, Acc 1, Acc 2, Other): Use the color pickers to define your style. Select a tool to paint that terrain type onto the grid.
Erase (Deep): Returns hexes to their default “Deep” state (or transparent state if an image background is active).
Outline: Paints traversable hex borders without filling the interior—ideal for marking paths on top of background images.

River & Platform

River Waypoints: Set the flow of the current. Click on the map to drop pathing nodes. The River will automatically fill the specified radius around your line.
Platform (⭐ Store Plat): Sculpt your ideal raft using terrain tools, select the area with the Select tool, and click Store Plat. This saves the shape as your permanent moving platform.

Selection & Buffers

Select: Drag to define a rectangular area.
Copy/Paste: Standard clipboard operations for your terrain.
Store 1: Save a prefab to a secondary memory bank.
Paste 1: Drops your stored prefab at the mouse location.

Canvas & Export

Resize: Change map dimensions (60x60 default).
Export HTML: Generates a standalone, interactive map file. This file contains all your logic, colors, and pathing and can be opened in any web browser without needing the editor.


🎮 Player Controls (Exported Map)
Once you have exported your map, open it in any browser. The interface is stripped back to focus on your session, with the following hidden hotkeys for live control:





























KeyActionA / EnterAdvance Platform along the river path.RReset View (centers the map and resets zoom).VReverse Current (toggles flow direction).HHide/Show River (toggles river path visibility).1 - 9Jump to Waypoint (instantly snaps platform to specific key nodes).

🎨 Advanced Theming Tips

Background Images: Use the Set BG button to upload a custom texture or map image. If an image is loaded, the engine will prioritize it as the backdrop.
Custom Deep Water: Use the Deep Color picker to tint the oscillating water effect to match your map’s biome (e.g., green for swamp, dark blue for abyss).

Pro-Tip: When exporting a map with a high-resolution background image, the resulting .html file size may increase as the image is embedded directly into the file for total portability.

Savage-Lands.title: Savage Lands
Savage-Lands.content:
Savage Lands
A vast, primal wilderness region beyond the more settled coasts of Emberfall. Characterized by:

Extreme abundance of Primals (both animal and plant)
Oversized, aggressive wildlife
Dense jungle and mesa terrain
Overwhelming magical vitality

The true source of this heightened state is a continual leak of raw Primal Energy from a wounded ancient Gold Dragon deeper inland. The leak was caused by Malazar, who left one of his own claws embedded in the dragon’s underbelly.

Key Locations

Savage Spire — the primary Kin settlement and the surface expression of the primal leak
The inland region surrounding the Gold Dragon — where (Pierre) - Piero Fruosino di Antonio da Vinci is rooted
Various hunting grounds and migratory paths used by the Kin


Cultural Notes
The Kin (animal-bonded humans) of the region have adapted to live alongside Primals rather than dominate them. Survival requires understanding the amplified instincts of the local wildlife.
Herd movements have grown more frequent and larger in recent times — a direct symptom of the intensifying leak.

Related Pages

Savage Spire
The Mycelial Elder
(Pierre) - Piero Fruosino di Antonio da Vinci
Gold Dragon
Primal Energy
Primal Bond
Primals

Savage-Spire.title: Savage Spire
Savage-Spire.content:
Savage Spire
An immense mesa settlement in the Savage Lands, home of the Kin (animal-bonded humans) and the The Mycelial Elder.
From the surrounding waters the cliff face appears densely overgrown with jungle vegetation. Long bamboo stairways and hanging platforms climb toward the settlement above.
The Spire is heavily saturated with residual magical influence. Many inhabitants display subtle physical alterations from Primal Bonds: unusual eyes, altered skin, faint animalistic features, or other controlled adaptations.

The True Source of the Magic
The overwhelming magical saturation is not generated by the Spire itself.
It is the surface expression of a vast leak of raw Primal Energy coming from a wounded Gold Dragon deeper inland. The Spire and its people have adapted to (and learned to safely share) that excess energy over generations.

The Mycelial Network
A fungal-based communication and control lattice embedded directly into the Spire’s stone and the Kin’s biology.

Environmental Regulation: Used by the Elder to maintain the terraced jungles and oxygen flow.
Resonance Detection: Capable of “pinging” Primal energy signatures from miles away.
Emergency Containment: Can be weaponized to bind or stabilize volatile forces (e.g., the Pocket Door).

Structural Description
The Spire consists of three primary vertical zones, maintained by the specialized labor of the Kin:
1. Base Port Layer

Infrastructure: Cliffside docks, ladder networks, and vertical cargo lifts carved into the mesa walls.
Ecological Role: The interface for trade and Kin migration.
State: Labor cycles are slowing as the “Thinning” reduces the physical stamina of the porters.

2. Mid-Span Ecosystem Layer

Environment: Dense jungle growth across terraced rock formations.
Population: Animal-kin labor networks (avian, feline, and mixed Kin Mutanophemes).
Condition: Visible biological fatigue; the adaptive traits (climbing claws, sensory ridges) are becoming vestigial and brittle.

3. Summit Plateau

Environment: A prehistoric ecological zone kept in artificial balance.

Key Entity: The Mycelial Elder
The primary interface for the Spire’s ecology. The Elder is not a ruler but a Regulator. It maintains the containment lattice and manages the Temple Water Rituals necessary to halt the “Fade” of the Kin population.

Status of the Spire Kin
The Leopard-kin porters and Hawk-eyed guards are currently Thin-Blooded. After several generations without a Primal Integration, their “Mutanopheme” edge is receding.

Physical Strain: Signs of energy depletion and structural biological thinning.
Awe & Hunger: The Spire Kin sense the “Primal” (draconic) presence in the Heroes with religious reverence. To them, the party carries the “Source Code” required to trigger a New Bloom.


Key Infrastructure & Artifacts
The Temple Waters
Located at the summit, these hyper-conductive waters are the means of Primal Integration. They allow a concentrated essence (like a draconic infestation) to be “thinned” and shared among the cluster.

Narrative Role: The Symbiosis of the Burden
The Savage Spire represents a critical turning point for the Heroes. It is a live containment structure that has become an ecosystem.
The Moral/Mechanical Trade:
The Spire is no longer stable in isolation; it is fading. The Heroes possess an overwhelming Primal force that is killing one of their own. By performing the Water Ritual at the Spire:

The Infested Hero  Captain Killian is relieved as the burden is thinned and shared.
The Spire Kin are reinvigorated, halting the “Fade” and regaining their specialized forms.
The Spire itself is stabilized as the new Primal energy reinforces the Mycelial Network.


The Question: Will the party allow their “curse” to become the communal “blessing” that saves the Spire from becoming mundane?


Key Figures

The Mycelial Elder — primary interface consciousness of the upper vertical ecology; speaks for the Spire.
(Pierre) - Piero Fruosino di Antonio da Vinci — the “tree-man” rooted near the Gold Dragon; former researcher who crossed the Fool’s Curtain.


The Kin & Primal Bonds
Primals are creatures burdened by excess magical essence. Through an ancient controlled ritual, portions of that essence can be shared with humanoid hosts. This stabilizes the Primal while granting the bonded individual survival adaptations suited to the hostile jungle.
The relationship is treated as mutual survival, not domination.
No dragon-linked Kin exist within the Spire. Dragon essence is considered too volatile and too closely tied to Malazar.

Role in the Larger Plot
The people of the Spire will ultimately be asked to make a profound voluntary sacrifice: surrendering their own Primal Bonds so the unbound energy can return to the Gold Dragon as the “seed” needed to finally close its wound.
To them this is not loss of power. It is returning a sacred gift to its rightful source.

Related Pages

Session-14-Midpoint-Encounter.title: Session 14 Midpoint Encounter
Session-14-Midpoint-Encounter.content:
Encounter: The Claw Emerges (CR 9)
Timing: Mid-session
Tone: High threat, low HP, snappy (3–5 rounds)
Purpose: First real interaction with the gold dragon’s wound. Removes one aggressive piece of Malazar’s lingering will without fully solving the problem.
Setup
The party reaches the wounded Gold Dragon.
A long, jagged gash leaks raw primal energy (golden-green motes).
Pierre (or investigation) has already concluded: something is still lodged in the wound.
Trigger
Any serious attempt to examine, touch, heal, or magically interact with the gash causes the obstruction to react.
A wet tearing sound.
A single enormous, razor-sharpened black claw — clearly broken from a much larger dragon — rips free of the wound and rises into the air.

Creatures

1 × Malazar’s Severed Claw (CR 7)
2 × Overgrown Primal Beast (CR 4) — arrive at the start of round 2 (or already nearby)



Tactics


Claw prioritizes whoever is interacting with the wound.
Uses malice pulse early, then focuses Power Attack claw strikes.
Never leaves the wound area.


Overflow Beasts flank and trip. They are short-lived pressure.


If Savage Spire warriors are present, they fight with calm professionalism. Quiet comments only. One may simply observe: “The knife still has a pulse.”



Aftermath
When the Claw is destroyed it dissolves into black motes that the leaking energy slowly burns away.
That section of the wound visibly calms for a short time.
This does not close the wound.
It only removes one active piece of Malazar’s will.
The true obstruction remains deeper — a magical signature that only someone carrying Malazar’s own corruption can safely grasp and extract.
This sets up:

The need for deeper attunement to the curse
(Pierre) - Piero Fruosino di Antonio da Vinci’s knowledge + the heroes’ resonance
The eventual voluntary sacrifice of Primal Bonds by the Savage people

The-Mycelial-Elder.title: The Mycelial Elder
The-Mycelial-Elder.content:
The Mycelial Elder is the primary interface consciousness of the Kin systems within the upper vertical ecology of the Savage Spire.
It is not a single organism in the conventional sense, but a distributed fungal intelligence formed from generations of biological integration, environmental memory, and ritual stabilization protocols.
It speaks for the Spire.
And, in many ways, it is the Spire speaking back.

Role in the Campaign

Gatekeeper to upper Spire systems
Ecological stabilizer of the vertical Kin civilization
Interpreter of primal resonance and containment failure
Mediator between Heroes and mycelial infrastructure


Personality

Ancient
Soft-spoken
Occasionally forgetful in a “too-many-lifetimes-at-once” way
Warmly respectful toward outsiders
Slightly goofy in tone, as if humor leaks through fungal diffusion

Despite this tone, it is deeply respected.
Not feared.
Respected like weather is respected.

Appearance
The Elder manifests as:

A Kin-shaped figure partially dissolved into glowing fungal lattice
Bioluminescent veins threading through translucent flesh
Slow drifting spores that pulse with speech rhythms
Eyes that occasionally “lag behind” reality by a fraction of a second


Speech Style
The Mycelial Elder speaks slowly, warmly, and with odd comedic timing.
It often:

repeats itself gently
misunderstands modern idioms in strange but harmless ways
pauses mid-sentence as if consulting a forest of memories

It sounds old.
And a little silly.
But never ignorant.

Dialogue Samples
First Contact at the Vertical Port

“Ahhh… visitors. Yes. Many feet. Many decisions arriving at once. That is… statistically unfortunate for the ecosystem, but socially delightful.”


“Please do not step on the blue moss. It is currently thinking about becoming something important.”


On the State of the Spire

“The Spire is… how you say… overfull. Like a jar with too many thoughts inside and not enough forgetting.”


“We have been pruning reality gently for many years. Gently is important. Aggressive pruning makes the mushrooms anxious.”


On the Fool’s Curtain

“The Curtain is not evil. It is… accumulation. Like compost, but for history and regret.”


“Some things do not disappear. They just change their posture and wait.”


On Captain Killian

“Ah yes. The human in the pocket door. He is still here. Still insisting on being himself. Very persistent soul. Slightly inconvenient for entropy.”


“We are holding him gently. Like a cup that does not wish to break, but is also not entirely convinced it is a cup.”


On the Primal System Instability

“The Primal must be vented, yes. If not, it becomes… recursive. Like a thought that learns to think about thinking until it forgets what it was originally meant to do.”


“We prefer thoughts that stay polite.”


On the Heroes

“You are… unusual. You carry storm-memory in your bones.”


“That is either a blessing or a maintenance issue. We are still deciding which folder to place you in.”


Secrets (DM Only)

The Elder is aware the Spire is a containment structure, not a civilization
It has been deliberately slowing certain ecological failures to prevent cascade collapse
It recognizes Malazar-class corruption signatures as “ancient reuse patterns”
It may allow the party access to dangerous systems if it believes “humor is involved”
It is not fully certain whether it is one entity or many agreeing to speak politely


Hooks

May become a recurring advisor on primal resonance events
Could request the party perform “improper maintenance” on reality
Might eventually assist in stabilizing or severing the Fool’s Curtain
Has latent recognition of draconic aspect corruption in the party

Water-Ritual-Aftermath---Dragon-Boons.title: Water Ritual Aftermath - Dragon Boons
Water-Ritual-Aftermath---Dragon-Boons.content:
The draconic corruption carried by the Heroes was never intended to create six dragons.
It was intended to recreate one.
During the Temple Water Ritual, the corruption threatening to transform Captain Killian into a vassal of Malazar was interrupted, divided, and redistributed among the party. Rather than allowing a singular draconic possession to complete, the ritual fractured the essence into six conceptual aspects of draconic existence.
Each aspect represents not merely a physical mutation, but a metaphysical principle tied to the nature of dragons themselves.
As the bearers continue to use and rely upon these powers, the aspects deepen their attunement, physically and spiritually reshaping their hosts.
The powers are not gifts.
They are organs of a larger being attempting to reassemble itself through mortal vessels.


































AspectPrincipleWingsFreedomClawsViolenceScalesEnduranceEyesAwarenessBreathPowerHornsDominion

Structure of the Aspects
Each aspect progresses through three stages of attunement:
Stage I — Manifestation
The mutation first appears.
Minor physical changes and limited abilities emerge.
Stage II — Assimilation
The draconic instinct strengthens.
The bearer gains stronger abilities while their personality and body begin visibly changing.
Stage III — Realization
The aspect fully awakens.
The bearer becomes a living embodiment of that draconic principle.

Known Risks
Every use of these powers strengthens the lingering influence of Malazar.
The Deck of Draconic Will exists as the primary method through which the corruption attempts to exert influence over its hosts.
Repeated reliance upon the aspects may:

alter personality
harm you physically
damage your armor/weapons
invoke compulsions
accelerate mutation
weaken resistance to Malazar’s posession

A portion of the power of Killian’s Curse shared among the Heroes outside the Fool’s Curtain
These specific attunements carry base concepts conveyed in the Draconic Kin Attunement
Tier 1: Fledgling Wings
Your back bears the budding, leathery weight of black dragon wings. They are flightless and mostly downy, but they instinctively respond to your body’s physical movements.
Passives


Draconic Stride: You gain a permanent +5 ft bonus to your base land speed.


Cushioned Descent: The wings naturally flare out to catch the air when you drop. You reduce all falling damage by 1d6 (treating falls as if they were 10 feet shorter).


Draconic Balance: The wings act as a natural counterweight to your movements. You gain a permanent +2 bonus on Acrobatics checks.


Actives (Cost: 1 Daily Use)


Draconic Shroud: As a Swift Action on your turn, you wrap the dark, webbed wings around yourself to completely muddy your silhouette. You gain a +5 bonus on Stealth checks for 1 round.


Winged Obfuscation (Reaction): As an Immediate Action when targeted by an attack, you flare your wings to disrupt your silhouette and throw off your attacker’s aim.


No Concealment: You gain partial concealment (20% miss chance) against that specific attack.


Partial Concealment: It upgrades to total concealment (50% miss chance) against that specific attack.


Total Concealment: You automatically enter Stealth without needing to spend an action or roll a check, completely hiding your location from that attacker.


Restriction: This provides no offensive advantage on the triggering attack and cannot be used to instantly cause a Sneak Attack on the enemy’s turn.


Attunement ☐☐☐☐
Tier 2: Draconic Expansion
*The wings grow physically larger, and thick, midnight-black scales begin to harden across the limbs. Your physical control over them tightens as the curse disperses into raw power. *
NOTE: Tier 2 active abilities Attune you to your wings faster, awarding 2 attunement points per use
Passives


Draconic Stride: You retain your permanent +5 ft bonus to your base land speed.


Parachute Canopy: The expanding surface area catches the air with immense force. You reduce all falling damage by 2d6 (treating falls as if they were 20 feet shorter).


Draconic Balance: Your center of gravity becomes incredibly stable. You gain a permanent +4 bonus on Acrobatics checks.


Actives (Cost: 1 Daily Use)


Draconic Shroud: Functions exactly as Tier 1 (+5 bonus on Stealth checks for 1 round).


Winged Obfuscation (Reaction): Functions exactly as Tier 1.


Buffeting Escape: As a Move Action, you violently beat your growing wings to create a blinding burst of foul wind and acrid swamp dust while leaping backward. Make a Dirty Trick combat maneuver against a single adjacent enemy’s CMD, rolling 1d20 + your Stealth modifier + 2.


Success: The target is blinded for 1 round.


Movement: Whether the maneuver succeeds or fails against their CMD, you can immediately move up to 10 feet away without provoking an attack of opportunity from that specific enemy.


Attunement ☐☐☐☐☐☐☐☐☐☐
Tier 3: Sovereign Wyrm
The wings reach their absolute mature span, rippling with muscle and coated in impenetrable, acid-scarred scales. The foreign consciousness of the dragon is fully conquered, giving you total mastery over its ultimate forms.
NOTE: you are fully attuned to your wings
Passives


Draconic Stride: You retain your permanent +5 ft bonus to your base land speed.


True Glide: The wings are large enough to fully halt your terminal velocity. You reduce all falling damage by 3d6 (treating falls as if they were 30 feet shorter).


Draconic Balance: You move across narrow surfaces with supernatural grace. You gain a permanent +6 bonus on Acrobatics checks.


Sovereign Scale: The hardened black dragon hide fully matures.
You gain permanent Acid Resistance 5.


Actives (Cost: 1 Daily Use)


Draconic Shroud: Functions exactly as Tier 1 (+5 bonus on Stealth checks for 1 round).


Winged Obfuscation (Reaction): Functions exactly as Tier 1.


Buffeting Escape: Functions exactly as Tier 2.


Vortex Blast: As a Standard Action, you snap your massive dragon wings forward with explosive force, unleashing a violent hurricane gale in a 15-foot cone originating from you. Every creature caught in the cone must succeed on a DC 20 Reflex save or be knocked Prone by the crushing wind pressure.


Temporary Flight: As a Swift Action, you fully override the physical limits of your halfling frame and force the wings into a powerful, rhythmic beat. You gain a Fly speed of 40 feet (Good maneuverability) for 1 minute.

future-memory.title: future memory
future-memory.content:
narrative description of the Cyclopean ritual the Heroes perform, driven by Leon’s research into the cyclops scroll from Session 1
Phase I: The Offering of Memories
The scent of burning kindling mixes with the heavy, organic aroma of the crushed sheep’s heart, the sharp tang of dill, and salt. At the exact center of your circle lies the stone, resting over the offering. The silence is absolute.
One by one, you must approach the stone, touch its cold surface, and silently surrender your most significant memory—the anchor of who you are.


If a true memory is offered: The stone drinks the thought, pulsing a deep, vibrant green.


If the offering is half-hearted or false: The stone flashes an angry, jarring red. A cold, echoing voice rings directly inside your skull: “Try again. Nothing is free.”


Once the final, true memory is accepted, the stone shifts. It begins to glow with a pale, amber-yellow light, humming with a vibration you can feel in your teeth. In perfect sync, you step forward, join hands, and look down into the amber light.

Phase II: The Trade and The Descent
Looking into the stone is like peering through a glass viewport at first. You see a city of sprawling grandeur—Eldoni, the capital of Eldoria. But the view is fleeting.
Suddenly, your mind experiences a violent tearing sensation. You feel a core piece of your own past being physically dragged out of your consciousness. In its place, a heavy, uninvited memory forces its way in. Around the edges of your mind, only a faint, frustrating wisp of what you used to know remains. You cannot remember the old memory; you only know the void it left behind.
The viewport shatters. You aren’t looking down anymore. You are there.

Phase III: The Vision (The Four Steps)
Step 1: The Ruin of Eldoni
The transition is instantaneous. You are standing in a major thoroughfare of Eldoni, but the capital is breaking. A choking violet static fills the sky, and the roar of collapsing stone is deafening. You feel the weight of phantom armor and the suffocating terror of a battle already lost.  You are the last surviving member of your battalion,  looking for the other members of your company to begin a final attempt.
The spires which adorn the outer walls are smoking, the inner walls are crumbled, and you know that everything stands on this last moment.  Yet, the most terrifying part is the atmosphere. The city feels completely empty of life—no living birds fly, no stray animals scurry through the debris. Instead, a thick, greasy malice hangs in the air, a menacing and undefined evil watching from the shadows. You know instinctively that a great shadow is here, though you cannot see it.
The vision shifts.
Driven by panic and a sudden, burning need to find an answer, you all see through Leon’s determined eyes.  He views the city from a high balcony, then turns and sprints away from the fallen Eldoni, hurtling down the steps of a grand, crumbling tower. He descends into a subterranean library. As he runs, his eyes catch a massive, permanent mural on the wall: Balfour I and Malazar, side-by-side, signing a fateful contract.
Leon suddenly remembers he needs to find … something… something to stop this nightmare. But where is it? The moment his mind, all of your shared minds, focused on the need.  He steps once more down the hall, but this step whisks him away. The world warps around you.
Step 2: The Hearth
The library stretches, blurs, and snaps like a rubber band.
Suddenly, the smell of smoke and ash is gone. The air is quiet, rich with the rich, inviting aroma of baking bread and slow-simmering broth. You are standing inside a cozy, deeply lived-in home. The details here are hyper-sharp and solid.
Your gaze is pulled immediately to the stone mantlepiece over the crackling fireplace. Resting there is an object—something small and handheld, something unassuming yet radiating a dormant resonance. You share a moment of precient realization. This object is part of the solution. But it isn’t the only one. Where is the rest?  Your need drives the next step, and instead of walking to the hearth to learn more about this small object, another shift tears you from the scene.
Step 3: The Researcher’s Records Room
The warm cottage walls dissolve outward into shadow.
Your feet are suddenly resting on old hardwood. The air is thick with the scent of decaying parchment and old ink. You are in a private records room.  As you glance at the closest open scroll, you sense a familiarity to the writing and speech you read.
Shelves and tables are crammed with massive stacks of scrolls and heavy, leather-bound books. Roughly half of the room is organized into meticulous, neat piles. The other half, however, is a chaotic blur of activity. Open tomes are scattered face-down, scrolls have been hastily unrolled and left askew, and ink jars sit uncapped alongside frantic, half-finished notes. The space bears the unmistakable mark of its owner having rifled through it in a state of sudden, desperate urgency.
Just then, the same malice and dread from the beginning of the vision comes over you.  The oppressive, unseen malice from the burning city presses against the boundaries of this room, a reminder that time is running out. You need the final piece. Knowing this worked to get you here, you think of where it must be hidden and step into the need.
The shadows twist, pulling you forward one last time.
Step 4: The Tech Facility
The frantic records room blurs into clean, oppressive lines of cold steel and glowing ley-lines.
You are deep in the bowels of an arcane tech facility, located in the distant southwest corner of Eldoni. The silence here is clinical and absolute. You are standing at the end of a long, narrow room.
At the far end, resting at the end of a thin, austere bed used for the long nights in research, is a heavily padlocked chest. It hums with a volatile, locked-away energy.
Looking at that chest, a deep, instinctual certainty cements itself into your minds: This is one piece of a larger trinity. If you face the final battle in the capital without breaking into this facility and retrieving what is inside that chest first, Eldoni will burn, and the entity in the shadows will win.  Mist begins to cover your vision and the shadow which you fear draws you in.

Phase IV: The Wake
The vision snaps like a broken mirror.
With a violent, collective gasp, you are yanked backward. The sterile tech facility vanishes, replaced by the familiar crackle of your own campfires. You are back in the circle, still holding hands, your chests heaving for breath.
In the dead center, the meticulously placed rock has gone completely dark and cold. Beneath it, the mixture of dill, salt, and the sheep’s heart has been utterly consumed, reduced to nothing but a fine, pale white ash.
